title: "SAP template: diagnostic clinical performance study"
subtitle: "Blank structure with prompts. Fill each section; delete prompts."
---

Structure borrowed from ICH E9 (by analogy) and adapted to IVDR Annex XIII Part A 2.3.2 and ISO 20916:2019. See `sap_ptau217_mock.qmd` for a filled example.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Document ID / version / date | |
| Protocol / CPSP reference | |
| Author, independent reviewer, approver | |
| Applicable SOPs | |
| Version history and lock date (before unblinding of reference-standard data) | |

## 1. Objectives and hypotheses
- Intended use and intended-use population (as in labelling).
- Primary objective; each primary endpoint with a **performance goal** and a pre-specified success rule.
- Secondary and exploratory objectives.

## 2. Design, reference standard, cut-offs
- Design (prospective, banked, case-control; sites; settings).
- **Reference standard**: definition, readers/adjudication, blinding both ways, timing window, handling of unreadable results.
- **Cut-offs**: how and where derived, lock date and file, rule for indeterminate results, convention at the boundary (≤ vs <).

## 3. Analysis populations
- Enrolled, **evaluable (primary)**, per-protocol. State the diagnostic analogue of ITT: who is in, who is out, why.

## 4. Endpoints and statistical methods
- Each endpoint: definition, numerator/denominator, CI method (Wilson, exact, other), software function.
- Treatment of indeterminates: separate category, counted as non-agreement, excluded in a sensitivity analysis.
- Prevalence dependence of predictive values.
- Agreement metrics when the comparator is not a reference standard: PPA/NPA/OPA (FDA 2007).

## 5. Sample size
- Assumed expected performance, goals, alpha, power, category frequencies, loss to non-evaluable; method and cross-check.

## 6. Missing, invalid and unreadable results
- Repeat rules, exclusion rules, flow diagram (STARD), worst-case and imputation sensitivity analyses.

## 7. Subgroups
- List (age, sex, kidney function, cognitive status, setting, other), minimum n for reporting, descriptive vs inferential.

## 8. Multiplicity, interim analyses, sensitivity analyses
- Co-primary rule, hierarchy, adjustments; interim analyses (if any) and who sees what; sensitivity analyses list.

## 9. Data standards
- Datasets (SDTM/ADaM-style by analogy; CDISC device implementation guides exist), derivations, controlled terminology.

## 10. Software, validation and QC
- R version, `renv.lock`, validated functions and tests; double programming of primary endpoints; QC checklist.

## 11. Tables, figures, listings (shells)
- Disposition, baseline, 3×2 table, primary, secondary, subgroups, sensitivity, listings of discordant cases.

## 12. Deviations and amendments
- How deviations are recorded; amendment procedure after lock.
